claims.statement: Vercel documents the prefix vcp_ for Vercel personal access tokens.

sources.supports: As part of this change, we've also updated token and API key formats to make them visually identifiable. Each credential type now includes a prefix: vcp for Vercel personal access tokens
Personal access tokens begin with the prefix vcp_, and the value will not be shown again.

claims.statement: No Vercel page read on 2026-10-06 states a length for the vcp_ token. Pinned scanner rules by different maintainers (Kingfisher (MongoDB), Betterleaks and CredSweeper (Samsung)) all fix 56 characters after the prefix (Kingfisher as a 50-character body plus a 6-character checksum), and the one provider example carries a 56-character body: vcp_ example in the Vercel CLI global options page (its body ends with the word EXAMPLE, so it is hand-written). This is consistency of the artifacts with 56, not a Vercel rule; the Kingfisher and Betterleaks examples reproduce the same documented example value, so their agreement on the example is not independent evidence of the length.

sources.supports: vcp_(?P<body>[A-Za-z0-9_-]{50})(?P<checksum>[A-Za-z0-9]{6}): a 50-character body and a 6-character checksum after the prefix
vcp_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{56}: 56 characters after the prefix
vcp_[0-9A-Za-z]{56}: 56 characters after the prefix
vcp_ example in the Vercel CLI global options page (its body ends with the word EXAMPLE, so it is hand-written)

claims.statement: The alphabet of the body is not settled. The pinned rules disagree: Kingfisher admits _ and - in the first 50 characters and only [A-Za-z0-9] in the last 6; Betterleaks admits _ and - throughout; CredSweeper admits only [0-9A-Za-z] and refuses a following _ or -. Vercel's own Azure DevOps extension masks vcp_ followed by [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ with no length. Every Vercel example read is alphanumeric. No Vercel page states an alphabet.

sources.supports: .replace(/vcp_[A-Za-z0-9_-]+/g, "vcp_***")

claims.statement: Pinned scanner rules are consistent with the contract grammar (3 artifacts: CredSweeper; betterleaks; kingfisher).

sources.supports: betterleaks: vc[pikar]_ + 56 [A-Za-z0-9_-] (derived from kingfisher)
kingfisher: vc[pikar]_ + 50 [A-Za-z0-9_-] + 6 [A-Za-z0-9] (Base62 CRC-32 tail)
CredSweeper: vcp_ + exactly 56 [0-9A-Za-z] (samples fail the checksum, so independent of kingfisher)

claims.statement: checksum: the last 6 characters may be base62 (0-9A-Za-z) of the CRC-32 of the 50 before them (Not enforced and never a twin: positives carry a matching and a mismatching tail.)

openQuestions.question: Does Vercel state the length of a vcp_ token anywhere (an API reference, a changelog entry, a support article)? Until it does, 56 characters after the prefix rests on scanner rules and one example.
May the body contain _ or -? The scanner rules and Vercel's own masker admit them; the examples do not use them. A Vercel statement of the alphabet would settle it.
